correctness.rationale: Closed-neighborhood identification means sixteen distinct nonempty signatures. The universal bound 2^4-1=15 proves that five sensors are necessary in the Shrikhande graph; a representative size-five code has sixteen explicitly tabulated valid signatures. Translation and twelve linear Cayley automorphisms yield the 96 distinct geometric templates. The exhaustive 4368-size-five subset test proves these are all optima. Parity-coset intersection invariants and nonadjacent common-neighbor pairs then identify each optimum exchange component with C6. The rook minimum of six is independently checked and previously published; two reproducible complete enumerators obtain precisely 2208 rook optima, 28800 exchange edges and, by BFS from each optimum, eccentricity six at all 2208 states. Both scripts independently construct the SRG graphs and reproduce all numerical and geometric claims, with exact small finite universes and no sampling.

originality.rationale: The 2008 primary paper proves the rook identifying-code number but neither the Shrikhande optimum classification nor exchange-graph geometry. The 2015 primary paper addresses identifying codes and bounds in vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs and reproduces the Cartesian clique result without these exact findings. Related publicly recorded calculations on the same pair concern different invariants (independence complexes, Cech complexes, zero forcing, metric resolving sets, bootstrap activation), with no reduction implying identifying-code signatures or optimum sensor-exchange components. Targeted literature and published-result comparisons found no covering result; unindexed equal computations remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A computational code table or equivalent result under alternative terminology might be unindexed or inaccessible.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact question motivated by identification/sensor-location coding: minimum cardinality, classification of all optima and whether one sensor may be relocated while retaining optimal distinguishing power. The Shrikhande graph hits the universal logarithmic information bound with five vertices while its parameter-twin rook graph requires six. More than a numerical gap, the affine parity-coset classification yields sixteen mutually unreachable optimal six-cycle configuration families, whereas all 2208 rook optima form one connected diameter-six graph. The finite and geometric structural contrast is meaningful despite the limited graph order; it is not merely a re-evaluation of the published rook minimum or a generic textbook deduction.
